topic: Why is the whole world dependent on chips from Taiwan?
title: Why Almost Every Advanced Chip Comes From One Island
description: One company in Taiwan, TSMC, makes about 70% of the world's contract-made chips — for Apple, Nvidia and AMD.
A 2021 study put 92% of the most advanced (sub-10 nm) chipmaking capacity in Taiwan.
sources: Focus Taiwan / TrendForce – TSMC held 69.9% of the global foundry market in 2025: https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202603130009

SIA & BCG – Strengthening the Global Semiconductor Supply Chain (2021): 92% of capacity below 10 nm in Taiwan, 8% in South Korea: https://www.semiconductors.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/BCG-x-SIA-Strengthening-the-Global-Semiconductor-Value-Chain-April-2021_1.pdf
Tom's Hardware – Apple A17 Pro: 3 nm, 19 billion transistors: https://tomshardware.com/news/apple-a17-pro-3nm-iphone-15-pro
HWBusters – ASML is the only maker of EUV lithography machines; TSMC builds chips for Nvidia, Apple and AMD: https://hwbusters.com/news/the-quiet-monopoly-powering-every-advanced-chip-in-the-world/

beats.narration: The chip in your phone was probably made on one small *island*.
Taiwan. Home to TSMC, which builds chips for Apple, Nvidia and AMD.
TSMC alone makes about *70%* of the chips that companies order from factories.
And for the most advanced chips, a 2021 study put Taiwan's share at *92%*.
A phone chip like Apple's A17 Pro packs *19 billion* transistors.
And their factories rely on machines that only one Dutch company in the world can build: ASML.
So one small island quietly builds the brains inside the devices you use every single day.
